newsitem.title: USA: DLJ president's 96 pay tops $33 mln - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: DLJ president's 96 pay tops $33 mln - WSJ.

text.p: Joe Ruby, the president of Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Inc, was paid more than $33 million in 1996, plus stock options, the Wall Street Journal said in its electronic edition Wednesday.
The report, based on the company's proxy statement, said Roby's pay is the biggest total compensation on Wall Street so far and is 78 percent more than the $18.6 million Roby received in 1995.
The report said Roby's pay topped that of Bear Stearns Cos Inc Chairman Alan Greenberg, who received $19 million in cash and stock last year.
It said DLJ Chairman and Chief Executive John Chalsty received a compensation package of $11.3 million last year, down from $17.5 million in 1995.
